entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:3
segments:
Bread of affliction; in remembrance of their afflictions in Egypt. 
 
We should not forget our past trials, nor the goodness of God in our deliverance, but should be encouraged by his kindness to put our trust in him, and with patient continuance in well-doing look to him for all we need.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:6
segments: Such is the unteachableness of men, that the Lord sees it needful often to repeat his instructions, especially with regard to their guilt as sinners, and their need of pardoning mercy through the atonement of Christ.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:9
segments: To put the sickle; to reap the sheaf of first-fruits, which was offered on the first day of unleavened bread.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:11
segments: True religion is social in its character, and tends to make all who possess it grateful, kind, communicative, benevolent, and joyful.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:17
segments: Religious joy and gratitude to God may at suitable times be properly expressed by feasting on the bounties of his providence, and giving them liberally to the poor and destitute.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:19
segments:
Wrest; pervert. 
 
  A gift; a bribe, something given to make a judge partial. 
 
  Doth blind the eyes of the wise; to truth and equity.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:20
segments: Civil government is God's institution to secure to men those rights and privileges which it is his will that they should enjoy; and magistrates are bound, as far as practicable, to give to all what justly belongs to them.

entries.title: Deuteronomy 16:21
segments: Grove; the word in the original rather means a wooden image of Astarte, fixed in the ground.  See
